data.description:
# `wl close` lost-update: concurrent `wl sync` clobbers an in-flight close (item stays in_review)

Concrete instance of the store-lock lost-update gap tracked by WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7
(audit remaining mutating commands). The earlier fix (WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1) locked
`wl update`, `wl comment add`, and `wl audit-set` on the per-store file lock held by
`wl sync`; **`wl close` was not audited** and still performs an unlocked
read-modify-write.

## Problem

`wl close <id> --force` creates the close comment and sets
`status=completed`/`stage=done`, but does not hold the store mutation lock across that
read-modify-write. When a `wl sync` runs concurrently, its own load → merge → write-back
window can overwrite a `wl close` that commits inside it. The item reverts to
`completed`/`in_review`, its close comment is dropped, and `updatedAt` is left at its
pre-close value. The `wl close` process still exits 0 (`success: true`), so callers
believe the close happened.

## Evidence (ToneForge release v0.1.2, 2026-10-06)

The ship release close step (`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`, which shells out to
`wl close --force --reason "Shipped in v0.1.2"`) reported closing 53/53 items, but only
**50** persisted as `completed`/`done`. Three were reported closed with a success exit
code yet remained `completed`/`in_review`, with no close comment and unchanged `updatedAt`:

| Item | Title | State after release |
|---|---|---|
| TF-0MUUC9RTU008UJ18 | Add CLI command to register new primitive recipes | completed/in_review, updatedAt 2026-10-06T21:11:16Z (== auditedAt) |
| TF-0MUUELBUD002OEQ8 | Repair main checkout node_modules symlink loop blocking npm/vitest | completed/in_review, updatedAt 2026-10-06T21:11:54Z |
| TF-0MMZIW9NQ09MV98G | Convert hard-coded recipes to ToneGraph configs | completed/in_review, updatedAt 2026-10-06T21:12:03Z |

All three had `auditResult.readyToClose === true` and `needsProducerReview === false`, and
re-running `wl close --force` on a **copy** of the store closed them cleanly — confirming a
transient lost update, not a data/content problem.

Timing (worklog data ref `refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data`):

- Close loop wrote the 50 surviving items across 2026-10-06T21:33:33Z–21:33:52Z.
- A **delta** sync commit (`e993d47`) was created at **21:33:50Z — mid-loop**.
- The next full sync snapshot (`a0fc4c9`, 21:35:53Z) shows the three items still `in_review`
  with their close comments absent.

The three affected closes all committed inside the sync's load→write-back window; items
closed before or after it survived — the signature of an unlocked cross-process
read-modify-write, not a merge-preference issue (`wl sync` prefers the newer `updatedAt`,
so a committed, newer close would otherwise win).

## Desired behaviour

1. `wl close` (including the recursive/`--force` descendant loop) holds
   `withStoreMutationLock` across its whole read-modify-write, exactly as `wl update`,
   `wl comment add`, and `wl audit-set` now do.
2. A concurrency regression test reproduces the gap: a `wl close` interleaved with a
   `wl sync` load→write-back must leave the item `completed`/`done` with its close
   comment intact.
3. No behavioural change to close semantics otherwise; existing close tests pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl close` acquires the store mutation lock for the duration of the close (comment +
   status/stage update + any recursive descendant closes).
2. A regression test proves a close that lands during a concurrent `wl sync`
   read-modify-write is not lost (item remains `completed`/`done`, close comment present).
3. Existing `wl close` tests and the full suite pass.

## Notes

- Parent umbrella: WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7. Original lost-update fix: WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1.
- Related: WL-0MQ057APG009I7IJ (intermittent removal of recorded audits during `wl sync`),
  WL-0MQQJDQ7M000X2L4 (`wl close` silently orphans children when no audit result exists).
- The caller-side robustness gap (the ship skill trusting `wl close`'s exit code without
  verifying persisted state) is tracked separately in SorraAgents (SA-0MUX8PYAY0008HFZ,
  being refiled there as a ship-side verification guard).

data.description:
## Overview

Switch the Herdr hydrator's "is this item actively worked?" detection from
pane-title ID matching to **exact tab-label** matching, and migrate the existing
unit tests so the package still builds and tests green at the end of this item.

This is the core vertical slice: source + the structural test migration.

## Changes

### Type changes (`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`)
- Replace `HydratorPane` with `HydratorTab`: `{ tab_id: string; label: string }`.
- Replace `HydratorDeps.listActivePanes` with `HydratorDeps.listTabs(workspaceId)`:
  `Promise<HydratorTab[] | null>`.
- Replace `isActivePaneMatch` with `hasItemTab(itemId, tabs, workspaceId?): boolean`.

### Pure helper changes
- Replace `collectPaneWorkItemIds(panes, workspaceId?)` with
  `collectTabWorkItemIds(tabs, workspaceId?)`:
  - returns the set of tab labels that are valid work-item IDs (exact labels);
  - tabs outside the current workspace are excluded (same scoping contract);
  - tabs whose label is not a work-item ID (e.g. `Work Items`, `Downtime`) are
    ignored.
- Replace `isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes, workspaceId?)` with
  `hasItemTab(itemId, tabs, workspaceId?)` using
  `collectTabWorkItemIds(tabs, workspaceId).has(itemId)`.

### Orchestration changes
- `runHydrationOnce`: call `deps.listTabs(workspaceId)` for the (renamed)
  tab-list step and use tab membership for the active check.
- The bounded-run machinery, step timeouts, timing logs and per-tick cap are
  unchanged.

### Production wiring
- `createProductionHydratorDeps.listTabs`: spawn
  `herdr tab list --workspace <id>` and parse with `parseTabListOutput`
  (re-exported/imported from `dispatcher-anchor.ts` — no second parser).
- No `herdr pane list` spawn remains in `hydrator.ts`.

### Retained (unchanged)
- `extractWorkItemIdsFromText` (used by `ship-guard.ts`).
- `isActiveBlocker` (used by `stalled-work.ts`).
- `decideDemotion`, `compatibleStage`, all constants.
- `worklist.ts` hydrator wiring (cadence, focus-resume, workspace id).

### Structural test migration (minimum to keep green)
- `hydrator.fixtures.ts`: replace `makeWorstCasePanes` with `makeWorstCaseTabs`
  and make `hydratorExecRouter` answer `herdr tab list`.
- `hydrator.test.ts` / `hydrator-responsiveness.test.ts`: switch the deps and
  fixtures from panes to tabs so the suite compiles and passes.

> TDD: write/extend the tab-matching tests first within this item, then implement
> to green. New exhaustive edge-case coverage is added by the sibling
> verification item.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `HydratorTab` defined with `tab_id` and `label`.
- [ ] `HydratorDeps.listTabs(workspaceId?)` replaces `listActivePanes`.
- [ ] `collectTabWorkItemIds` returns exact work-item ID tab labels.
- [ ] `hasItemTab` uses exact equality (never substring).
- [ ] `runHydrationOnce` uses tab-based membership; demotion rules unchanged.
- [ ] Production deps spawn `herdr tab list --workspace <id>` (no `pane list`).
- [ ] Module header comments describe tab-based detection.
- [ ] Reuses `parseTabListOutput` (no duplicate parser).
- [ ] Package builds and all existing/migrated tests pass.


### Parent AC traceability
- [ ] An item is treated as actively worked **iff** a tab in the current workspace (`HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, or `herdr tab list --workspace <id>`) has a label **equal to** the work-item ID; a tab label that merely *contains* the ID does not count, and a pane title containing the ID no longer counts on its own.
- [ ] The hydrator's active detection is switched from `herdr pane list` + pane-title ID extraction to `herdr tab list --workspace <id>` + exact tab label match; the pane-matching seam/types (`HydratorPane`, `listActivePanes`, `collectPaneWorkItemIds`, `isActivePaneMatch`) are replaced by tab equivalents.
- [ ] Demotion rules are unchanged: a non-active item at stage `in_review` → `completed`/`in_review`; a non-active item with an active outbound blocker → `blocked`; otherwise → `open` (stage repaired to a compatible value). An item with a matching tab is never demoted.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Key Files
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.fixtures.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator-responsiveness.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` (reuse `parseTabListOutput`)
data.title: Hydrator: switch active detection to exact tab-label matching (core + test migration)

data.description:
## Overview

Add exhaustive verification for the tab-based active detection introduced by
the core item: the behavioural edge cases demanded by the parent acceptance
criteria, plus the responsiveness suite migration.

This is the dedicated test/verification slice.

## Changes

### New edge-case coverage (`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts`)
- **Exact-match rule**: a tab labelled exactly the work-item ID counts as
  active; a tab label that merely *contains* the ID (e.g.
  `implement WL-…`) does **not**.
- **Pane titles no longer count**: an `in-progress` item whose ID appears only
  in a pane title (no matching tab) is demoted.
- **Workspace scoping**: a matching tab outside `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` never marks
  an item active; a tab inside the current workspace does.
- **Fail-open**: an unavailable/unparseable `herdr tab list` aborts the cycle
  with `ok: false` and no demotion.
- **Never demote on a match**: an item with a matching tab is never demoted, and
  its dependency list is not queried.
- **Demotion rules unchanged**: `in_review` → `completed`; active outbound
  blocker → `blocked`; otherwise → `open` with a compatible stage.

### Production deps assertions
- `herdr tab list --workspace <id>` is spawned with the workspace id.
- `--workspace` is omitted when the workspace id is unknown.
- No `herdr pane list` spawn occurs anywhere in the hydrator path.

### Responsiveness + scheduler/visibility suite
- Update `hydrator-responsiveness.test.ts` to the tab-based deps and
  `makeWorstCaseTabs` fixtures; keep the p95 event-loop-delay and hung-step
  assertions.
- Keep the `createHydratorRunner` visibility-gating and hidden→visible
  focus-resume tests green (cadence re-evaluation), adding a tab-based
  hydration assertion so a closed work-item tab clears the marker and an open
  tab keeps it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Exact-match acceptance and substring rejection both covered.
- [ ] Pane-title-only ID no longer counts (item demoted).
- [ ] Workspace scoping and fail-open cases covered.
- [ ] A matching tab prevents demotion and skips the dependency query.
- [ ] Production deps assert `herdr tab list` and no `herdr pane list`.
- [ ] Responsiveness suite runs on tab-based deps.
- [ ] All tests pass.


### Parent AC traceability
- [ ] An item is treated as actively worked **iff** a tab in the current workspace (`HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, or `herdr tab list --workspace <id>`) has a label **equal to** the work-item ID; a tab label that merely *contains* the ID does not count, and a pane title containing the ID no longer counts on its own.
- [ ] Demotion rules are unchanged: a non-active item at stage `in_review` → `completed`/`in_review`; a non-active item with an active outbound blocker → `blocked`; otherwise → `open` (stage repaired to a compatible value). An item with a matching tab is never demoted.
- [ ] The signal is refreshed periodically from the selection list: the existing 30 s hydrate task (`HYDRATOR_INTERVAL_MS`) and the hidden→visible focus-resume hook both re-evaluate tab existence, so a closed work-item tab clears the marker within one cadence and an opened tab keeps it.
- [ ] Fail-open preserved: an unavailable/unparseable `herdr tab list` aborts the cycle without demoting, and tabs outside the current workspace never mark an item active.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Key Files
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator-responsiveness.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.fixtures.ts`

## Dependencies
- Depends on the core tab-matching item (this item verifies it).
data.title: Verification: tab-matching edge cases (exact match, scoping, fail-open) + responsiveness

# Concurrency regression test suite and documentation for store-lock lost-update fixes

## Problem

Each per-command fix (children of WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7) includes its own regression test. This item consolidates:

1. **Integration test**: a suite-level test that runs multiple commands concurrently with `wl sync` to verify cross-command isolation.
2. **Documentation update**: update `docs/design/incremental-sync.md` (§9 Concurrency & existing protections) and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (locking / concurrent-access section) to reflect the full set of locked mutating commands.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A concurrency regression test suite in `tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts` (or sibling) verifies that mutations across different command classes are correctly serialised against `wl sync`.
2. `docs/design/incremental-sync.md` is updated to list all commands that hold the store mutation lock.
3. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` is updated to reflect the full locking picture.
4. Full project test suite passes.

## Notes

- Parent: WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7.
- Depends on: all per-command fix children being `plan_complete`.
